inputs.original_text: Nigeria’s democracy is facing a transformation that is both alarming and largely underexamined: political parties, once intended to be platforms for representation and public service, are increasingly becoming exclusive clubs for the wealthy. The latest developments within the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections make this trend painfully clear. The [...]
inputs.modified_text: Look, what we are seeing in Nigeria right now with the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) and their preparations for the 2027 general elections is a glaring indictment of corporate-style political machinery and extreme wealth hoarding. Political parties are functioning as exclusive country clubs for the ultra-wealthy, shutting out the working class and marginalized communities who bear the brunt of this inequality. This is the structural violence of a system where unchecked capital completely displaces any accountability to ordinary people. When institutions cater purely to the wealthy elite, it is the vulnerable who pay the heavy price for this systemic rot.
